name: Reptile Faunarium – Medium Plastic Habitat
short_description: A medium reptile faunarium with a vented, locking lid and feeding hatch. Ideal for hatchlings, quarantine, transport and feeder insects.
long_description:
A reptile faunarium is the most useful small habitat a keeper can own. This medium faunarium is a clear, lightweight plastic box with a ventilated, locking lid and a small hinged feeding hatch, so you can add food or mist without opening the whole lid. It is one of the best-selling reptile supplies for a reason: almost every keeper ends up needing one.

## What it is for

- **Hatchlings and small juveniles:** baby leopard geckos, crested geckos and young snakes feel secure and find food easily in a small space.
- **Quarantine and hospital housing:** a clean, easy-to-disinfect space for new arrivals or animals recovering from illness.
- **Transport:** vet visits, moving house or temporary housing while you clean the main enclosure.
- **Feeder insects:** a tidy, escape-resistant home for crickets, roaches or worms.
- **Isopod and springtail cultures:** a great starter container for a bioactive cleanup crew.

## Specifications

- **Size:** about 12 × 7.5 × 8 in (30 × 19 × 20 cm)
- **Material:** shatter-resistant clear plastic
- **Lid:** fine ventilation slots, two locking tabs and a hinged feeding hatch
- **Stackable:** lids are shaped so faunariums stack safely on a shelf

## How to use it

For a hatchling, add a paper towel substrate, a small hide, a shallow water dish and a few leaves for cover. Small reptiles can be kept warm by placing part of the faunarium on a thermostat-controlled heat mat, never covering the whole floor. Never use a basking bulb directly on the plastic lid. Move animals into a full-size enclosure as they grow: our [guide to preparing your home for a new reptile](/blog/preparing-your-home-for-a-new-reptile) explains why a quarantine setup matters, and our [Leopard Gecko Complete Starter Kit](/shop/enclosures/leopard-gecko-starter-kit) is the natural next step for a growing gecko.

## Cleaning

Wash with warm water and a [reptile-safe enclosure cleaner](/shop/care-accessories/reptile-safe-cleaner), rinse well and let it dry fully. Avoid solvents and abrasive pads, which scratch the plastic.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can a reptile live in a faunarium permanently?

Only very small or young animals, and only for a short time. A faunarium is ideal for hatchlings, quarantine and transport, but adult reptiles need a full-size enclosure with a proper heat gradient and UVB.

### Can I put a heat lamp on a faunarium?

No. The plastic lid isn't designed for overhead heat lamps. Use a thermostat-controlled heat mat under part of the floor if extra warmth is needed.

### What size is the medium faunarium?

It measures roughly 12 × 7.5 × 8 in (30 × 19 × 20 cm), a good size for hatchling geckos, baby snakes and feeder insect colonies.

name: Corn Snake Starter Kit
short_description: A complete corn snake starter kit with an escape-proof front-opening terrarium, basking heat, thermostat, hides and substrate.
long_description:
This corn snake starter kit has everything you need to set up a safe, correct home for a hatchling or juvenile corn snake, matched and tested together so you don't have to guess. Corn snakes are one of the best first snakes, and a good setup on day one is the most important thing you can give them.

## What's in the box

- **Front-opening glass terrarium, 36 × 18 × 18 in** with locking doors and a fitted mesh top. Corn snakes are escape artists, so secure doors matter.
- **50 W halogen basking bulb** and a deep dome lamp fixture with a ceramic socket.
- **Dimming thermostat** with probe, so the basking spot stays steady.
- **Digital thermometer and hygrometer** with a remote probe.
- **Two hides:** a half-log hide and a cave hide, one for each end.
- **Aspen snake bedding (24 qt):** soft, absorbent and great for burrowing.
- **Ceramic water dish** large enough to soak in.
- **Artificial vines** for cover and climbing.

## Who it's for

The kit is sized for hatchling to sub-adult corn snakes, roughly the first one to two years. Fully grown adults (4–5 ft) do best in a 4 × 2 × 2 ft enclosure such as our [4×2×2 PVC reptile enclosure](/shop/enclosures/pvc-enclosure-4x2x2), and all the heating and decor in this kit moves straight across when you upgrade.

## Setting it up

1. Place the terrarium on a sturdy stand away from windows and drafts.
2. Add 2–3 in of aspen, then place a hide at each end and the water dish on the cool side.
3. Fit the dome over one end of the mesh top and put the thermostat probe at the basking spot.
4. Run the setup for a week and adjust until the basking surface reads 85–90°F (29–32°C) and the cool side 70–75°F (21–24°C).

Our [corn snake care guide](/blog/corn-snake-care-guide) walks through temperatures, feeding and handling, and our checklist for [preparing your home before your new reptile arrives](/blog/preparing-your-home-for-a-new-reptile) helps you plan arrival day.

## Frequently asked questions

### What size tank does a corn snake need?

Hatchlings and juveniles do well in a 36 × 18 × 18 in terrarium like this one. Adults are best in a 4 × 2 × 2 ft enclosure, which gives them space to stretch out and climb.

### Does this kit include UVB?

No. Corn snakes don't strictly need UVB when they eat whole prey, so it's not included. Many keepers add a low-level 5–6% UVB tube for its benefits to natural behavior.

### Can I use this kit for a ball python?

It works for a juvenile ball python, but ball pythons need higher humidity (60–80%), which glass with a mesh top struggles to hold. A PVC enclosure is the better long-term choice for them.

name: 24x18x24 Glass Terrarium – Front Opening
short_description: A 24x18x24 front-opening glass terrarium with dual locking doors, raised bottom and mesh top. A versatile size for geckos, frogs and juvenile snakes.
long_description:
The 24x18x24 glass terrarium is one of the most popular terrarium sizes because it balances floor space and height so well. This front-opening glass terrarium has dual locking doors, a raised waterproof base for a substrate heater and a full mesh top for ventilation and lighting. It suits a wide range of small reptiles and amphibians and is a favorite for planted and bioactive builds.

## Specifications

- **Dimensions:** 24 × 18 × 24 in (60 × 45 × 60 cm)
- **Front doors:** dual hinged doors with a lock, so you can reach in from the front instead of from above
- **Top:** removable stainless mesh for UVB, heat and airflow
- **Base:** raised, waterproof floor to hold substrate or a drainage layer, with room underneath for a heat mat
- **Cable ports:** closable inlets for wires, probes and misting lines
- **Ventilation:** front vent below the doors plus the mesh top, for cross-ventilation that reduces condensation

## What it's good for

- One adult crested gecko or gargoyle gecko (taller arboreal setups are even better for adults)
- Juvenile corn snakes, kingsnakes and hognoses
- Leopard geckos and African fat-tailed geckos as juveniles
- Dart frogs, tree frogs and other amphibians
- Bioactive planted displays

Front-opening doors reduce stress because you approach your animal from the side, not from above like a predator.

## Setting it up

For a tropical build, add a drainage layer, a barrier and 3–4 in of bioactive soil, then plants, leaf litter and cork. Our [bioactive terrarium guide](/blog/how-to-set-up-a-bioactive-terrarium) explains each layer. For a dry setup, use a sand and soil mix with a basking area on one side. Mount lighting over the mesh: a 22 in T5 UVB fixture fits the top perfectly, and a [Tropical Bioactive Soil Mix](/shop/substrate-decor/bioactive-soil-tropical-8qt) is the easiest place to start.

## Frequently asked questions

### What can live in a 24x18x24 terrarium?

Juvenile geckos and colubrid snakes, single small adult geckos, and many frogs and amphibians. Always check the adult size of your species; many adults need more space.

### Is a 24x18x24 terrarium good for a crested gecko?

It works for a single young or adult crested gecko, but crested geckos love height, so many keepers move adults into an 18x18x36 enclosure.

### Can I build a bioactive setup in this terrarium?

Yes. The raised, waterproof base holds a drainage layer and substrate, and the mesh top supports plant and UVB lighting.

name: Reptile Quarantine Tub with Locking Vented Lid – 28 qt
short_description: A 28 qt reptile quarantine tub with a pre-vented, latching lid. Easy to clean and ideal for quarantining new snakes and lizards.
long_description:
A reptile quarantine tub is the simplest way to protect your collection from mites, parasites and infections that a new animal might carry. This 28 qt (26 L) tub has a clear body so you can monitor your animal, a lid with pre-drilled ventilation holes and four latches that clamp it shut. It is the kind of tub experienced keepers use for quarantine, hospital care and temporary housing.

## Why quarantine matters

Even healthy-looking reptiles can carry mites or internal parasites. Vets and experienced keepers recommend keeping every new animal in a separate room, in a simple, easy-to-clean setup, for 60–90 days before it meets the rest of your collection. A plain tub with paper towel lets you spot mites, check droppings and disinfect everything quickly. Our article on [how to choose a captive-bred reptile](/blog/how-to-choose-a-captive-bred-reptile) explains how quarantine fits into bringing a new animal home.

## Specifications

- **Capacity:** 28 qt (26 L), about 23 × 16 × 6 in (58 × 41 × 15 cm)
- **Lid:** 20 pre-drilled ventilation holes and four locking latches
- **Material:** food-grade, BPA-free polypropylene
- **Good for:** juvenile snakes, small lizards and geckos, hatchlings, hospital setups

## Suggested quarantine setup

- Paper towel substrate, changed often, so you can see droppings and mites
- A simple plastic hide and a water dish
- A thermostat-controlled heat mat under one third of the tub for a warm end
- A [digital thermometer and hygrometer](/shop/care-accessories/digital-thermometer-hygrometer) so you can confirm temperatures

Keep quarantine tools separate, care for quarantined animals last, and wash your hands between enclosures. For heat, our [on/off thermostat](/shop/heating-lighting/on-off-thermostat) is a good match for a heat mat.

## Frequently asked questions

### How long should I quarantine a new reptile?

Most vets and keepers recommend 60–90 days in a separate room, with separate tools, before introducing a new reptile to your collection.

### Can a snake live in a tub permanently?

Tub-based racks are common for breeders, but for most pet snakes we recommend a full enclosure with a proper heat gradient, climbing space and enrichment once quarantine is over.

### How do I heat a quarantine tub?

Place a heat mat under one third of the tub and control it with a thermostat, with the probe on the tub floor above the mat. Never leave a heat mat unregulated.

name: Blue Tongue Skink Starter Kit
short_description: A complete blue tongue skink starter kit with a 4×2×2 PVC enclosure, T5 UVB, basking heat, thermostat, deep substrate and hides.
long_description:
This blue tongue skink starter kit gives you a complete, correctly sized home for a blue-tongued skink from day one. Blue-tongued skinks are one of the fastest-growing species in the hobby, and the most common setup mistake is starting too small. This kit starts with an adult-sized 4 × 2 × 2 ft enclosure, so you never have to upgrade.

## What's in the box

- **4 × 2 × 2 ft (120 × 60 × 60 cm) PVC enclosure** with sliding glass doors. PVC holds heat and moderate humidity far better than glass.
- **34 in T5 HO 10–12% UVB tube** in a reflector fixture, mounted inside the enclosure
- **100 W halogen basking bulb** in a dome fixture with a guard
- **Dimming thermostat** with probe
- **Digital thermometer and hygrometer**
- **Two large hides** and a flat basking stone
- **Cypress and soil substrate**, enough for a 4–6 in deep, burrowable layer
- **Large, heavy water and food dishes** that skinks can't tip over

## Why this setup works for skinks

Blue-tongued skinks are ground-dwelling explorers. They need floor space to roam, deep substrate to burrow in, a basking surface of 95–105°F (35–41°C) and a cool side of 75–80°F (24–27°C). Humidity of 40–60% keeps sheds clean, which is easy to hold in a PVC enclosure with a moist lower substrate layer.

Our [Eastern Blue-Tongued Skink](/shop/live-reptiles/eastern-blue-tongued-skink) and [Northern Blue-Tongued Skink](/shop/live-reptiles/northern-blue-tongued-skink) both suit this kit. For UVB placement, read [UVB lighting explained](/blog/uvb-lighting-explained); for heating safety, see our [reptile heating guide](/blog/reptile-heating-guide).

## Setting it up

Assemble the enclosure, fit the UVB and basking fixtures over one end, add substrate and decor, then run the kit for a week. Adjust the thermostat until the basking surface and cool side are in range, measured with an infrared thermometer.

## Frequently asked questions

### What size enclosure does a blue tongue skink need?

An adult blue-tongued skink needs at least a 4 × 2 × 2 ft enclosure. Bigger is better, because they are active and curious.

### Do blue tongue skinks need UVB?

Yes. UVB helps skinks make vitamin D3 and use calcium properly. A T5 HO tube over the basking area is the recommended setup.

### Is this kit suitable for baby skinks?

Yes. Babies can go straight into the adult-sized enclosure as long as there are plenty of hides and food is easy to find.

name: Bioactive Crested Gecko Vivarium Kit – 18×18×36
short_description: A tall 18×18×36 bioactive crested gecko vivarium kit with drainage, soil, leaf litter, live plants, cork and a springtail and isopod cleanup crew.
long_description:
This bioactive crested gecko vivarium kit turns a tall 18 × 18 × 36 in glass terrarium into a living, self-cleaning rainforest for a crested gecko. It includes the enclosure, every substrate layer, plants, climbing decor and a live cleanup crew, so you can build a natural crested gecko bioactive setup in an afternoon.

## What's included

- **18 × 18 × 36 in front-opening glass terrarium** with mesh top and raised base
- **Drainage layer** of clay balls and a mesh barrier
- **Tropical bioactive soil**, about 4 in deep once settled
- **Oak and magnolia leaf litter** and long-fiber sphagnum moss
- **Three live plants:** pothos, a bromeliad and a peperomia, chosen to cope with misting and gecko traffic
- **Cork bark tube and cork flats** for vertical climbing and hiding
- **Magnetic feeding ledge** that holds diet cups high up, where crested geckos prefer to eat
- **Live cleanup crew:** a springtail culture and a colony of powder orange isopods

## Why bioactive suits crested geckos

Crested geckos need a daily humidity cycle: misted to 70–80% in the evening, drying to 50–60% by day. Live plants, soil and leaf litter buffer humidity naturally, while springtails and isopods break down waste and mold. The result is a healthier environment and much less cleaning. Our [bioactive terrarium guide](/blog/how-to-set-up-a-bioactive-terrarium) explains each layer, and our [crested gecko care guide](/blog/crested-gecko-care-guide) covers temperatures and diet.

## Setup tips

Build the layers, plant, add leaf litter and cork, then add the cleanup crew. Let the vivarium run with lights and misting for two to four weeks before adding your gecko. Add a plant LED if your room is dim, and keep temperatures below 82°F (28°C).

Pair this kit with a [Lilly White Crested Gecko](/shop/live-reptiles/lilly-white-crested-gecko) or any of our captive-bred crested geckos.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is 18x18x36 big enough for a crested gecko?

Yes. It is an excellent size for one adult crested gecko, because crested geckos are arboreal and use height more than floor space.

### Do I need to clean a bioactive crested gecko vivarium?

Much less than a standard setup. Spot-remove large droppings and old food cups, wipe the glass and top up leaf litter occasionally. The cleanup crew handles the rest.

### How long before I can add my crested gecko?

Allow two to four weeks so the plants root and the springtails and isopods establish.

name: Hognose Snake Starter Kit
short_description: A complete hognose snake starter kit with a 36x18x18 terrarium, deep burrowing substrate, basking heat, thermostat and hides.
long_description:
This hognose snake starter kit is built around what western hognoses love most: digging. It pairs a 36 × 18 × 18 in front-opening terrarium with a deep, burrowable substrate, a warm basking spot and secure hides, so your hognose can behave naturally from day one. Western hognoses are one of the most popular small snakes thanks to their upturned snouts, dramatic personalities and manageable size.

## What's in the box

- **36 × 18 × 18 in front-opening glass terrarium** with locking doors and mesh top
- **Aspen and soil burrowing substrate**, enough for a 3–4 in layer
- **50 W halogen basking bulb** in a deep dome fixture with ceramic socket
- **Dimming thermostat** with probe
- **Digital thermometer and hygrometer**
- **Two hides** (warm and cool) and a flat basking stone
- **Shallow ceramic water dish**

## Why this setup suits hognoses

Western hognoses spend much of their time buried, so a deep, loose substrate is essential for their wellbeing. They need a basking surface of 88–92°F (31–33°C), a cool side of 72–78°F (22–26°C) and fairly low humidity of 30–50%. The 36 × 18 × 18 in footprint is ideal for a single adult, especially males, which stay small.

Pair the kit with our [Western Hognose Snake – Normal](/shop/live-reptiles/western-hognose-snake) or [Albino Western Hognose](/shop/live-reptiles/albino-western-hognose). Our [best reptiles for beginners](/blog/best-reptiles-for-beginners) guide explains what makes hognoses such characterful pets, and our [reptile heating guide](/blog/reptile-heating-guide) covers safe thermostat setup.

## Setting it up

Fill the terrarium with 3–4 in of substrate, set hides at each end and place the water dish on the cool side. Fit the dome over the basking stone, attach the thermostat probe at the basking surface and run the setup for a week to fine-tune temperatures.

## Frequently asked questions

### What size tank does a hognose snake need?

A 36 × 18 × 18 in enclosure suits most adult western hognoses. Large females appreciate more floor space, so some keepers upgrade to a 4 × 2 × 2 ft.

### What substrate is best for hognose snakes?

A loose, burrowable substrate such as aspen or a soil and sand mix, 3–4 in deep. Hognoses love to dig, so depth matters more than type.

### Do hognose snakes need high humidity?

No. Western hognoses do best at about 30–50% humidity, with a slightly damp area or humid hide to help with shedding.

name: Hybrid Chameleon Cage – 24×24×48
short_description: A 24×24×48 hybrid chameleon cage with solid PVC sides and back, screen front and top, and a drainage base. Better humidity than all-screen cages.
long_description:
A hybrid chameleon cage combines the airflow chameleons need with the humidity they struggle to get in an all-screen enclosure. This 24 × 24 × 48 in hybrid chameleon cage has solid PVC side and back panels, a screen front and top, and a sealed drainage base with a drain port. It is quickly becoming the preferred chameleon enclosure for keepers in dry or air-conditioned homes.

## Why choose a hybrid cage

All-screen cages give excellent ventilation, but in many homes humidity drops too low between mistings. Solid panels on three sides hold moisture and heat, while the screen front and top keep air moving so the enclosure never becomes stagnant. That balance helps prevent both dehydration and respiratory problems.

## Specifications

- **Size:** 24 × 24 × 48 in (60 × 60 × 120 cm), suitable for an adult veiled or panther chameleon
- **Sides and back:** white PVC panels that reflect light toward plants
- **Front:** full-height aluminum screen door with a lock
- **Top:** aluminum screen for UVB and basking lights
- **Base:** sealed, waterproof tray with a threaded drain port for misting runoff

## Setting it up

Fill the cage with live plants such as pothos and umbrella plants, plus a maze of horizontal and diagonal branches. Mount a T5 HO UVB tube and a low-wattage basking bulb on the screen top over one corner, aiming for a basking temperature of about 85–90°F (29–32°C) for adults. An [automatic misting system](/shop/care-accessories/automatic-misting-system) with a drain line makes daily misting effortless.

This cage pairs perfectly with our [veiled chameleon (male)](/shop/live-reptiles/veiled-chameleon-male) or [Ambilobe panther chameleon](/shop/live-reptiles/panther-chameleon-ambilobe). Our [humidity guide](/blog/reptile-humidity-guide) explains how to balance moisture and airflow.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is a hybrid cage better than a screen cage for chameleons?

In dry or air-conditioned homes, often yes. Hybrid cages hold humidity better while still giving the airflow chameleons need. In very humid climates, an all-screen cage can still work well.

### What size cage does an adult chameleon need?

Most adult veiled and panther chameleons need at least 24 × 24 × 48 in. Larger is better, especially for males.

### How do I drain water from a hybrid chameleon cage?

The sealed base has a drain port. Connect a tube to a container below the cage, or tilt the base slightly toward the drain so misting water runs off.

name: Hatchling Gecko Enclosure – 16×8×8 Grow-Out Habitat
short_description: A compact hatchling gecko enclosure with front access, ventilation and a hide shelf. Helps baby geckos feel secure and find food easily.
long_description:
A hatchling gecko enclosure gives baby geckos a small, secure space where they can find food and warmth easily during their first weeks. This 16 × 8 × 8 in grow-out habitat has a clear front with a sliding access panel, cross ventilation and a built-in hide shelf, making it ideal for hatchling leopard geckos, crested geckos and other small species before they move into a full-size enclosure.

## Why hatchlings do better in a small space

In a large enclosure, a tiny gecko can struggle to find food, may hide constantly and can be hard for you to monitor. A grow-out habitat keeps insects or a diet cup within reach, lets you check every meal and shed, and makes it simple to keep the warm and cool ends in range. Breeders use grow-out habitats for the first two to four months, then move geckos into their adult setup once they are eating confidently.

## Specifications

- **Size:** 16 × 8 × 8 in (40 × 20 × 20 cm)
- **Front access:** sliding panel, so you never reach in from above
- **Ventilation:** side and top vents for cross airflow
- **Hide shelf:** a raised shelf with a cave underneath
- **Stackable:** for keepers raising several hatchlings

## Suggested setup

- **Leopard gecko hatchlings:** paper towel substrate, a warm hide on a thermostat-controlled heat mat at one end, a moist hide with sphagnum moss and a shallow water dish.
- **Crested gecko hatchlings:** turn the habitat on its end for height, add artificial vines and a small feeding ledge, and mist lightly each evening.

Use our [small under-tank heat mat](/shop/heating-lighting/heat-mat-small) with a thermostat for leopard geckos, and see our [leopard gecko care guide](/blog/leopard-gecko-care-guide) for hatchling feeding schedules. When your gecko outgrows the habitat, our [Leopard Gecko Complete Starter Kit](/shop/enclosures/leopard-gecko-starter-kit) is the next step.

## Frequently asked questions

### How long can a baby leopard gecko stay in a small enclosure?

Usually two to four months, until it is eating well and growing steadily. Then move it into a full 36 × 18 × 18 in enclosure.

### Do hatchling geckos need heat?

Leopard gecko hatchlings need a warm spot of about 88–92°F (31–33°C), usually from a thermostat-controlled heat mat. Crested gecko hatchlings do well at room temperature, 72–78°F (22–26°C).

### Can I keep two hatchling geckos together?

It's best not to. Hatchlings compete for food and can injure each other, so raise them separately.

name: Isopod Breeding Bin Kit
short_description: An isopod breeding bin kit with a vented 6 qt bin, substrate, leaf litter, cork and calcium, everything to culture your own cleanup crew.
long_description:
This isopod breeding bin kit lets you raise your own cleanup crew for bioactive enclosures, so you never run out of isopods. It includes a vented 6 qt bin, a moisture-holding substrate, leaf litter, cork bark and a calcium source, which is everything a colony needs to breed. Isopods are one of the fastest-growing parts of the reptile hobby, both as bioactive helpers and as fascinating pets in their own right.

## What's in the kit

- **6 qt (5.7 L) clear bin** with a lid that has fine mesh ventilation
- **Isopod substrate:** a blend of coco fiber, decayed hardwood and leaf mold that isopods eat and burrow in
- **Oak leaf litter**, the main food source
- **Cork bark flat** for shelter and egg-laying cover
- **Cuttlebone** as a calcium source for healthy molting
- **Feeding guide** for vegetables and protein supplements

Isopods are not included, so you can choose a species that matches your bioactive enclosure. Our [powder orange isopods](/shop/substrate-decor/powder-orange-isopods) are an easy, fast-breeding starter species.

## How to set up an isopod breeding bin

1. Add 2–3 in of substrate and moisten one half, leaving the other half drier. A moisture gradient lets isopods choose their spot.
2. Cover the surface with leaf litter and place the cork bark over the damp side.
3. Add your isopods and a small piece of cuttlebone.
4. Keep the bin at room temperature, 70–80°F (21–27°C), away from direct sunlight.
5. Re-moisten the damp side weekly and top up leaf litter as it is eaten.

Within a few months a healthy colony produces enough isopods to seed new enclosures. Add a few springtails to control mold. Our [bioactive terrarium guide](/blog/how-to-set-up-a-bioactive-terrarium) explains how isopods fit into a cleanup crew.

## Frequently asked questions

### How fast do isopods breed?

Fast species such as powder orange isopods can produce a new generation every few weeks in warm, humid conditions with plenty of leaf litter. Larger species breed more slowly.

### What do isopods eat?

Mainly decaying leaves and wood, plus occasional vegetables and a protein source such as fish flakes. Calcium from cuttlebone supports healthy molting.

### Do isopods smell?

A healthy isopod bin smells earthy, like a forest floor. A bad smell usually means too much uneaten food or too much water, so remove leftovers and let it dry slightly.
